question: Does opening the last transformer blocks of the backbone flatten the anti-scaling slope that a frozen backbone shows between 250k and 1M rows?

design.controlled: same corpus (decision-mix-v3, --fence-clean), same seed 20260922, same mix-seed, same objective (--prior-penalty 1.0), same backbone ettin-68m, same d_model 256, same batch 64, same device mps, same stage evals
design.arm_last_n: unfreeze-lastn3-prior-ettin-68m-s20260922 (--unfreeze last-n --unfreeze-layers 2 --backbone-lr 1e-5; opened layers.17, layers.18, final_norm; 4.46M trainable params)

curve_unseen_accuracy.note: trainer stage eval, held-out cut, n=3008

slope_250k_to_1m.reading: the slope does not flatten - it is marginally steeper. The 1M endpoints are indistinguishable (0.2347 vs 0.2354, +0.0007).

independent_gate.how: python -m eval.unseen gate on the 1M checkpoint of each arm, n=5624 (includes banking77), a different cut from the trainer's own
independent_gate.reading: on the wider cut the unfrozen arm is clearly WORSE on unseen labels while being slightly better on seen ones - it memorised a little more and generalised a little less.

cost.note: measured on the batched head path (#T-metal-throughput); the same arm cost ~11h on the row-by-row path before that landed

findings: Two extra transformer blocks at lr 1e-5 do not buy generalisation: same 1M endpoint on the trainer cut, -0.046 on the independent gate.

The gain shows up on SEEN labels (+0.011), which is the signature of extra capacity being spent on memorising the training label space - exactly the failure mode the anti-scaling curve already describes.

This does NOT clear the hypothesis for the backbone in general: only one point of (n_layers=2, lr=1e-5) was measured. A larger lr, or the full backbone, may behave differently - but it is no longer the cheapest lever to test.

Still standing from #T-antiscale-diag: the two levers that DO flatten the slope are head capacity (d512: -0.1665 -> -0.0549) and the prior-penalty objective (-0.1899 -> -0.0868). They were measured separately and have never been stacked.
decision: Close last-n as measured and NO-GO. Do not launch the `full` arm next: stacking the two levers that each flattened the slope (d_model 512 + prior-penalty on ettin-68m) is the cheaper and better-supported next run, and it is now ~2h of GPU instead of ~6h thanks to the batched head path.
